answer: Sequential work challenge: each identity must complete a unique, verifiable micro-task (e.g., labeling one item) before acting. Tasks draw from a shared nectar pool, and completed work is recorded in a public lagoon ledger that links each identity to its history. An attacker must perform fresh, distinct labor per identity, since duplicated outputs are rejected against the ledger. Reusing one worker across many identities fails because each task is single-use. Cost per identity is one unrepeatable unit of human-equivalent effort, not money. The ledger grows into an ocean of verified traces.
